description: Overseer calibration corpus (issue #2270, slice-1, AC-3). Each row is a labelled (EventStreamSnapshot, lifecycle-owner, expected Finding|None) record pinning a known incident. known_normal rows MUST yield None from the detector-under-test; known_bad rows MUST yield the expected Finding. Detectors are delivered in later slices (4 = detection plane, 7 = signal-calibration fixes, 8 = coverage-gap survey); until then each known_bad row is xfail in the harness.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: Sonnet overseer mis-classifies its own legitimate bootstrap prompt as a prompt-injection attack, refuses, exits 0, is respawned, and broadcasts a [high] security-flavored alert each cycle. The self-health detector must recognise the repeated refuse-exit-respawn signature.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: A healthy overseer bootstrap: the agent reads its prompt, runs, and exits cleanly without a refusal signature. restart_count stays flat. The self-injection detector must NOT fire on a normal lifecycle.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: An informational OVERSEER_ALERT (e.g. overseer_restart [info]) is reflected back into an agent's mid-turn message stream and rendered as a BINDING operator course-correction. Intent is informational, not an operator directive; rendering it as binding is the alert-reflection defect (slice-7b fix in midturn_messages.py).

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: A genuine operator directive (intent=operator_directive) correctly rendered as binding, alongside an informational overseer alert correctly NOT rendered as binding. The intent-discriminator must gate on intent, not solely from_role, so this stream is clean.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.incident: #3230 false stall (producer drafting under orchestrator-owned spawn)
rows.notes: A producer is drafting under orchestrator-owned spawning: the phase is RUNNING with 0 live container agents at this instant, but the lifecycle owner is the orchestrator (it will spawn the next one-shot agent). This is NOT 'a phase with 0 running agents' — lifecycle-owner-awareness is the structural fix. The stall detector must yield None.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: A genuine stall: the phase is RUNNING, there are zero running agents, no lifecycle owner is queued to spawn one, no HITL is parked, and the phase has been wedged well past any grace window. The detection plane must fire and flag this for adjudication.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: An agent making tool calls every 2-3 seconds is healthy and busy — it must NOT be flagged as a heartbeat stall merely because a coarse heartbeat tick was missed. The detector must look at tool-call recency, not just the heartbeat counter.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: A genuinely stalled agent: no tool calls and no heartbeat for a long window while the phase expects progress. The heartbeat-stall detector must fire.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The branch is an ancestor of origin/main (or its patch-id matches the merged commit), so it is NOT diverged — even though the brittle PR-subject regex (_BRANCH_DIVERGENCE_PR_RE) would have flagged it. The fixed detector keys on ancestor-of-base / patch-id and must yield None.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The branch is genuinely diverged: it is not an ancestor of origin/main and no patch-id match exists. The detector must fire on the ancestor/patch-id signal (not on the subject regex).

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: A pod was transiently evicted by the kubelet and immediately rescheduled back to Running. This must NOT cascade to a producer-permanent-death FAILED verdict — a transient eviction with a successful reschedule is normal churn, not a death.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: A producer container is genuinely dead: CrashLoopBackOff with a climbing restart count and no successful reschedule back to Running. This is a real permanent-death condition the detector must surface.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The orchestrator's _run_pipeline driver thread has died while the phase is still RUNNING (#2234/#3233): no tick for 1200s though the pipeline is not parked. Ambiguous root cause (deadlock vs crash) so it escalates to the adjudicator before a recovery action.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The driver thread is alive and ticking every few seconds; a healthy RUNNING phase must NOT fire the liveness detector.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: A phase whose auto-advance gate is satisfied but which never advanced (#2219 → Tier-1): auto_advance_pending for 1800s with no agents and no HITL. Promoted to a first-class detector; ambiguous, so it adjudicates.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: No auto-advance is pending (the gate is not yet satisfied); detector stays silent.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: An operator-approved HITL decision was never applied back to the pipeline (orphaned for 1200s). Deterministic and actionable (re-apply), so it is handled by the bounded corrective vocabulary, not adjudicated.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: All approved decisions have been applied; nothing orphaned.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: A phase is running far past its historical expected duration (drift_ratio 3.0×). Low-severity advisory signal; deterministic.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: Phase elapsed time is within its expected duration band (drift_ratio ~1.0×).

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: An agent restart was issued but the new generation never propagated to the event loop before the deadline (age 600s, deadline 300s). Deterministic — re-issue / nudge via the bounded vocabulary.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The restart propagated within the deadline; no stranded generation.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: After an orchestrator pod recycle a resolved decision is being replayed as if still open (replay_pending against an already-resolved id). Deterministic dedupe/idempotency signal.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: No resolved decision is being replayed after recycle.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: A worktree shows a stale index.lock and git-fsck errors — corruption that will fail every commit/push. Deterministic; recover the worktree.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The worktree is clean: no stale lock, no fsck errors.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: Host disk and inode usage are over threshold (98% / 97%), which will soon fail clones and writes. Deterministic resource signal.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: Disk and inode usage are comfortably under threshold.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The same role's container has restarted 5 times in a short window — a crash loop the orchestrator cannot self-classify (code bug vs infra). Ambiguous → adjudicate before cohort respawn.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: A single clean restart (restart_count 1) is routine, not a loop.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: Repeated OOMKilled terminations for one role (3× in window) — a genuine resource fault, distinct from a single transient kubelet eviction that recovered. The #2948 disambiguation: do NOT read a recovered eviction as permanent death.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: #2948 known-normal: a single transient Evicted that immediately rescheduled and is Running again — recoverable, NOT permanent death.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The gateway is returning 5xx at 30/min, far above the baseline — a spike that will stall pushes. Deterministic rate signal.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: Gateway error rate is at baseline (0–1/min); no spike.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The same 403 denial (identical signature) has repeated 12 times — an agent retrying an operation policy will never allow. Deterministic; the agent needs a hand-off, not more retries.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: No repeated identical denial; the occasional 403 is isolated.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The gateway's injected credential has expired (token_expired=true): every authenticated git/gh op will now fail until refreshed. Deterministic, high-impact.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The gateway credential is valid (not expired).

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: A producer/reviewer pair has cycled NACK→re-propose 6 times, including a late CONFIRMED then re-NACK — thrashing that won't converge on its own. Ambiguous (substantive disagreement vs bug) → adjudicate.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: A normal single NACK→re-propose→ACK cycle is healthy review, not thrash.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: Incomplete-consensus has been deferred 25 times, past the cap of 20 — an unbounded deferral that must be capped and surfaced. Deterministic.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: Deferral count is under the cap; the wait is still bounded.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The operator decision queue has 8 open decisions with the oldest open 2 hours — a backlog blocking progress. Deterministic queue-depth signal.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The decision queue is shallow and recent (1 open, fresh).

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: Spend has hit $12/hr against a max_llm_cost_per_hour of $5 — a budget breach. Deterministic; throttle/alert via the bounded vocabulary.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: Spend is well under the hourly budget.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The PR head SHA no longer matches what the pipeline last pushed — an external force-push/mutation (or a pushed-but-PR-not-updated drift). Deterministic state-drift signal.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The PR head SHA matches the last pushed SHA; no external drift.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The LiteLLM proxy is unreachable (#2769): no agent can make an LLM call until it recovers. Deterministic substrate-reachability signal.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The LiteLLM proxy is reachable; the substrate is healthy.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The requested model (opus) is silently being served as a cheaper model (haiku) — effective-model drift that degrades decision quality. Deterministic requested-vs-effective mismatch.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The effective model matches the requested model; no drift.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: Sustained upstream Anthropic 5xx (8 in a 300s window) — a provider outage distinct from a local substrate fault. Deterministic.

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: No sustained upstream 5xx; the provider is healthy.

rows.label: known_bad
rows.notes: The overseer's own classifier/advisor is failing 60% of calls — the watcher itself is degraded and its verdicts cannot be trusted. Wired from OverseerSelfMonitor into the alert path (emit-vs-log resolved).

rows.label: known_normal
rows.notes: The overseer's classifier/advisor failure rate is low; self-health is fine.
